answer: To keep a swarm from buying votes, require each identity to lease a scarce live slot and prove exclusive control of it. Every few epochs a random peer sends a short challenge to that slot; only a timely, key-signed reply renews the lease. A missed reply burns the deposit and frees the slot. A falcon hunts from one ledge. A second persona is a decorative plume on a relic of the first key, and when two slots share signing material both leases are slashed. Parallel clones then cost more than they earn.
